Lessons.Title: Reasoning About Angles (Part 2)
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will use known angles to reason about unknown angles and write equations to reason about unknown angles.
In this lesson, you use what you know about angles and your measurements to solve problems that are increasingly more complex and abstract. To find measurements of unknown angles, you need to look for structure in the diagrams, reason about the relationships of the angles (including writing equations to represent the relationships), and perform addition, subtraction, and sometimes division. The problems in the lesson can be solved in more than one way and in different orders, but a small handful of the angles can only be quantified after the values of some other angles are known.

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: How Many Do You See: Obtuse Angles (10 minutes); Activity 1: Shaded and Unshaded Angles (15 minutes); Activity 2: Info Gap: A Whole Bunch of Angles (20 minutes); Cool-down: Heart to Heart (5 minutes)
Corrected mathematical focus: Write an equation for the total of adjacent angles and subtract known values to find the missing angle.
Edulytics authored guidance: A right angle of 90° is partitioned into 62° and an unknown angle. Write x + 62 = 90 and solve x = 28. Check that the parts sum to the unchanged 90° turn.
First-party Cool-down (not publisher assessment): A straight angle has adjacent parts 71° and 53°. Find the remaining angle.
Images, drawing/protractor accuracy, partner tasks and the gated original publisher Cool-down require original task evidence and teacher/visual review.

2021 original source evidence from earlier local Our-CS inspection: In Shaded and Unshaded Angles the original right-angle figure labels one part 62°, hence shaded complement is 90°−62°=28°. The source also shows a straight angle partitioned into three including 71° and a shaded part; do not assign a numeric answer without all labels and the actual source figure. Information Gap: A Whole Bunch of Angles is a partner-card communication task; teacher checks explanations and unknown-value equations. Original warm-up asks pupils to count obtuse angles in a folded heart image.

Source timeline: Warm-up: How Many Do You See: Obtuse Angles (10 minutes); Activity 1: Shaded and Unshaded Angles (15 minutes); Activity 2: Info Gap: A Whole Bunch of Angles (20 minutes); Cool-down: Heart to Heart (5 minutes). WorkedExamples.Title: Original right-angle shaded part
WorkedExamples.Question: A right angle consists of an unshaded 62° sector and one shaded sector. How many degrees is the shaded sector?
WorkedExamples.Method: A right angle is 90°. Subtract the known 62° part.
Steps: The two sectors total the original right angle, so the shaded part is 28°.
WorkedExamples.Check: This 62° label is reported in the original 2021 student excerpt.
